national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (国家税务总局, 'SAT'), administering tax registration, VAT, enterprise income tax, invoice control, and export tax refunds under the Golden Tax Phase IV (金税四期) system, with enforcement through provincial, municipal, and county-level tax service bureaus and the unified Electronic Tax Bureau (电子税务局). Authoritative portal: https://www.chinatax.gov.cn; national service hotline: 12366. The entity CN_WFOE_LTD is a mainland Chinese wholly foreign-owned enterprise whose operative tax domicile is exclusively the PRC; the 'TW' flag in the composite key identifies Taiwan as the counterparty export market or investor reference and confers no Taiwanese tax residence on this entity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and obtain the Business License bearing the 18-character Uniform Social Credit Code (统一社会信用代码, 'USCC'), which is legally recognized as the taxpayer identification number (TIN) for all PRC tax purposes. Step 2: Tax registration is triggered automatically through the multi-certificate integration (多证合一) data-sharing reform; within 30 days of license issuance, the WFOE must complete supplementary filings via the e-Tax Bureau, including accounting/financial system and software filing, bank deposit account reporting, legal representative and controlling shareholder information, and payroll records. Step 3: Determine VAT status — general taxpayer (一般纳税人) or small-scale taxpayer (小规模纳税人); an exporter seeking output-VAT refunds must obtain general taxpayer status or export through a licensed agent, and must complete the Export Tax Refund/Exemption Filing (出口退（免）税备案) before the first export declaration. Step 4: Complete customs registration as an import/export consignee/consignor (海关进出口收发货人备案), effect the foreign trade operator automatic filing with the Ministry of Commerce, and open trade foreign-exchange settlement accounts with a SAFE-designated bank linked to the Trade in Goods Foreign Exchange Monitoring System. Step 5: Apply for the Fully Digital Electronic Invoice (数电票) quota through the SAT invoice platform. No statutory minimum paid-in capital applies (subscription-based registered capital system), and online retail of home hydroponics and gardening equipment does not require a statutory license or an import/export permit.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (no pass-through eligibility). The WFOE is a PRC resident enterprise (居民企业) taxed on worldwide income under the Enterprise Income Tax Law at the standard 25% rate, with foreign tax credit relief for overseas taxes on the same income. Territorial scope: worldwide taxation; not a tax-exempt zone. Preferential EIT regimes available: 15% rate for certified High and New Technology Enterprises; effective 5% EIT on qualifying taxable income for Small Low-Profit Enterprises (taxable income not exceeding RMB 3 million, employees not exceeding 300, total assets not exceeding RMB 50 million, policy extended to 31 December 2027); 15% rate for encouraged industries in Western Development regions. Outbound dividends to non-resident shareholders are subject to 10% withholding tax; the Cross-Strait tax arrangement with Taiwan is signed but not in force as a comprehensive double-taxation treaty and provides no general withholding reduction. The entity is a VAT taxpayer on domestic sales and a zero-rated exporter on qualifying exports; local surtaxes (urban maintenance and construction tax at 7%/5%/1% by locale, plus education surcharge 3% and local education surcharge 2%) are assessed on VAT actually paid.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: China has no check-the-box entity classification mechanism; all limited companies are statutorily taxable at the entity level. The available elections are: (1) VAT status election — entities with annual taxable sales below RMB 5 million may elect general taxpayer status, and existing general taxpayers with annual sales not exceeding RMB 5 million may elect conversion to small-scale status through the time-limited window extending to 31 December 2027 (small-scale levy rate 3%, temporarily reduced to 1% through 31 December 2027); (2) export tax method election — manufacturing exporters use the 'exemption, credit and refund' (免抵退) method, whereas trading/merchant exporters use the 'exemption and refund' (免退税) method; (3) cross-border e-commerce elections in comprehensive pilot zones — the 'exemption without invoice' (无票免税) election for export sales lacking valid input VAT invoices, and the deemed taxable income assessment for EIT at 4% of export sales revenue under SAT Announcement 2019 No. 36; (4) Small Low-Profit Enterprise EIT preferential rate claimed at the annual EIT settlement; (5) anti-hybrid and thin-capitalization rules — interest deductions are limited by the 2:1 debt-to-equity thin-capitalization ratio and by hybrid-mismatch restrictions under SAT Announcement 2017 No. 2 where the counterparty jurisdiction does not tax the corresponding interest income.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), with delegated verification authority to designated Foreign Exchange Banks
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains current-account RMB convertibility in principle, but capital-account movements remain restricted and require SAFE registration or pre-approval. Export e-commerce proceeds and service/current-account receipts are generally convertible after truthfulness review; however profit remittance by a WFOE is characterised as 'investment income remittance' and requires audited financial statements, tax clearance or tax payment certificates, a board resolution declaring distributable profits, and completion of the annual foreign investment information and balance-of-payments verification filings. Capital repatriation by deregistration remains a capital-account matter. Cross-border e-commerce sales received in foreign currency must be settled into a licensed bank or SAFE-registered payment institution; funds may not bypass the PRC banking system. Any Taiwan-side settlement flows remain subject to separate cross-strait banking rules, but the underlying WFOE treasury exposure is governed by PBOC/SAFE.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no blanket statutory surrender or mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts; exporters may retain foreign exchange in designated trade foreign-exchange accounts within approved quotas. However, the WFOE must repatriate export proceeds to China and reconcile them under SAFE's Goods Trade Foreign Exchange Monitoring System against the matching customs declaration. As a baseline rule, payment for goods exports should be collected within 30 days after export customs clearance unless a deferred-payment arrangement is filed with SAFE in advance. Settlement into RMB must be supported by genuine underlying trade documentation, platform settlement reports, customs manifests, and logistics evidence; accounts maintained with banks or third-party payment institutions must ensure that e-commerce receipts are at all times attributable to the exporter's own trade registration data.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High for cross-border e-commerce receivable collection through SAFE-licensed or SAFE-filed payment institutions such as Airwallex, Payoneer, WorldFirst/PingPong, and Stripe's local licensed acquiring partners; Low for using an unlicensed offshore EMI as the primary RMB clearing route. The chosen fintech/EMI must maintain a licensed PRC bank partnership, a valid anti-money-laundering programme, and either a money-service business licence in its home jurisdiction or a SAFE non-bank payment institution cross-border foreign-exchange business filing. The EMI cannot independently settle foreign e-commerce receipts into RMB without a licensed PRC bank or payment institution intermediating through segregated client-fund trust accounts. For direct Stripe/PayPal payout lines, the WFOE should instruct payouts to its corporate bank account via SWIFT, ensuring the beneficiary name exactly matches the SAFE-registered WFOE name and the remittance references include the e-commerce order reconciliation ID.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: As a baseline, a new WFOE must present its legal representative or properly authorised director/manager, together with the financial controller if the entity is foreign-controlled, for a physical branch interview at account opening. Original corporate documents, notarised incorporation certificates, the company seal, financial seal, legal representative seal and bank signature card must be registered in-person at the Chinese bank branch. Remote opening is not uniformly prohibited by PBOC regulations, but in practice most tier-1 PRC banks accept remote/video KYC only for existing clients, a wholly online application with a digital seal, or cases where the bank's approved e-KYC and video interview facilities are available. For a foreign-invested entity, the conservative compliance position is physical attendance plus certification of foreign shareholder documents; remote-only onboarding will normally be declined or elevated to a juristic-person risk review.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: opaque ownership chain, nominee shareholders, multiple offshore shell tiers or beneficial-ownership inconsistency
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate registry extracts from each jurisdiction, shareholding chain down to ultimate natural-person UBOs, notarised declarations disclaiming nominee or shell status, organisational chart, physical office lease, staff payroll records, investor resumés and a written explanation of the commercial rationale for holding the WFOE through the existing structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: source of registered capital cannot be verified as originating from the declared investor, or the remitting bank appears on sanctions/other watchlists
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SWIFT credit advice and bank statements from the direct investor's funding account, notarised board resolution approving the capital contribution, SAFE Foreign Investment Registration Certificate or FDI account opening confirmation, capital verification report from a PRC CPA, declaration that no third-party or sanctions-listed entity funded the contribution, and documentary source-of-wealth evidence for the investor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: e-commerce transaction flows inconsistent with declared low-risk profile, including high refund/chargeback rates, multi-currency settlement across platforms, or mismatch between platform storefront and registered trade scope
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Up-to-date platform seller verification certificates for Stripe, PayPal, Amazon or equivalent marketplaces, monthly settlement and payout reports, order management logs, product listing URLs, refund/chargeback trend reports, customs declarations for exported hydroponics equipment, logistics delivery tracking and a written business-model and end-customer description confirming that the products are lawful gardening/hydroponics equipment with no prohibited use.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: inability to evidence authority of signatories, residence status, or the existence of the physical business premises in China, or unverified use of an e-commerce payment aggregator as sanctioned intermediary
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Passport and PRC residence permit or valid visa for the authorised director, PRC national ID for resident finance manager, original power of attorney and bank-observed signature/seal specimen, notarised legalisation of the foreign investor's constitutional documents, payment-aggregator licence or bank partnership confirmation for the selected fintech route, and utility bills or lease agreement proving actual business premises.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound foreign direct investment capital must be injected through a bank-designated FDI Capital Account opened only after completion of SAFE Foreign Investment Registration. The remitting investor should issue a SWIFT wire referencing the WFOE name, the SAFE registration code, and the purpose code for foreign investment capital injection; the bank will debit the Capital Account into a RMB settlement account under the 'capital account payment use' monitoring system. Chinese transfer methods may use CIPS (RMB) or SWIFT (foreign currency), and the receiving bank must verify the investor identity, remittance instructions, capital verification, and compliance with the Negative List. All copies of the wire instructions, MT103 confirmations, bank credit advices and SAFE filings must be retained as part of the treasury compliance file. Funds may not be used before the required SAFE capital account registration and bank review are completed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements for procurement of inventory, equipment, components, freight and operating services may be executed through SWIFT MT103/MT202 outward payments, RMB CIPS transfers, or commercial letters of credit (MT700) issued by the WFOE's PRC advising bank. Trade remittances must be supported by genuine invoices, purchase contracts, customs records where physical goods are crossed, platform transaction references, and billing statements for digital services. Direct e-commerce marketplace settlements to overseas suppliers should be coordinated through the licensed bank or fintech payment institution using the relevant goods-trade or service-trade purpose code; disbursements to financial accounts, related-party payables, or personal accounts require additional economic-substance evidence. If a cross-strait Taiwan vendor is involved, the trade payment should be subject to normal PRC goods-trade procedures and retained records of the cross-strait invoice and shipping documents.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts with a SAFE-licensed PRC bank under the real-demand principle
FX swaps and currency swaps between CNY and USD/EUR/JPY/TWD where a genuine trade-related exposure exists
Plain-vanilla FX options used to hedge anticipated current-account receipts or payables
Cross-currency interest rate swaps where the WFOE has a qualified underlying cross-border loan asset or liability
Offshore NDF contracts available only through a licensed offshore bank for CNH exposure, but not as a substitute for onshore SAFE hedging rules
FX forward-linked trade finance facilities or invoice discounting arrangements embedded in the clearing rail

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' meeting and approval of financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company shareholders; Ministry of Economic Affairs registry only if a registrable change occurs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of each financial year; normally by 30 June for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Director liability and potential administrative fines may apply; Taiwan has no automatic annual strike-off solely for missing an annual meeting. Persistent statutory noncompliance may support dissolution or registry cancellation procedures after statutory notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 May to 31 May following the end of the income-tax year for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or non-filing may trigger statutory fines, assessed tax, late-payment interest, and tax investigation. No fixed annual filing period automatically triggers strike-off; prolonged corporate noncompliance may lead to separate dissolution or cancellation action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual withholding tax statements and income information reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally by 31 January following the relevant calendar year; additional reporting applies upon cessation or liquidation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late, incomplete, or inaccurate reporting may result in statutory penalties, reassessment, and interest. Repeated noncompliance may trigger tax enforcement but does not create an automatic annual company strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and CPA certification where legally required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Taiwan National Taxation Bureau and, where applicable, other competent authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Prepared for annual closing and completed before the annual corporate income tax filing deadline; CPA certification applies to companies meeting statutory criteria
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare or certify required accounts may result in administrative fines, tax adjustments, loss of evidentiary support, and increased audit exposure. No automatic annual strike-off applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Company registry amendment filing, if annual review identifies changes in directors, managers, registered address, capital, business scope, or other registered particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce, or competent local company registry authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within 15 days after the change requiring registration; Taiwan does not impose a routine annual return filing for ordinary private companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines may apply for late or omitted amendment filings. Continued failure after official orders may result in compulsory rectification, dissolution measures, or registry cancellation; there is no universal fixed annual strike-off deadline.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent CPA audit or certification is generally required for public companies and for private companies meeting statutory capital or other criteria, including the applicable paid-in-capital threshold commonly set at NTD 30 million or more. Separate tax certification rules may apply based on industry, revenue, capital, or filing status.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan public companies and specified entities use Taiwan-IFRS. Ordinary private companies generally use Taiwan Generally Accepted Accounting Principles, subject to applicable Company Act, tax, and industry requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not generally prescribe a standalone annual UBO confirmation filing for ordinary private companies. The company should review ownership, control, directors, and nominee arrangements annually and update its internal records and AML or banking disclosures upon any change. Share transfers should be reflected in the shareholders' register and supported by transfer documentation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Supervisors, where applicable
Accounting books and supporting financial records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 800-2,500 per year, depending on address, mail handling, nominee or local representative services, and filing support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 2,000-10,000 per year for a small private trading or e-commerce company; higher fees apply for statutory CPA certification, inventory complexity, related-party transactions, or cross-border operations
